newsitem.title: POLAND: SOCCER-SHEARER, SHERINGHAM TAKE ENGLAND CLOSER TO FINALS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SHEARER, SHERINGHAM TAKE ENGLAND CLOSER TO FINALS.

text.p: England moved a giant step closer to next year's World Cup finals in France when they defeated their old rivals Poland 2-0 in a tough group two qualifer on Saturday.

A fifth minute goal from Alan Shearer and a second in the closing seconds from Teddy Sheringham mean that England cannot finish lower than second in the group which either they or Italy will win. At the same time, the result eliminated Poland.
Even if England do finish second, they now have an outstanding chance of the best record of all nine European runners-up, which carries with it automatic qualification for the finals.

The result leaves Italy on top of the standings with 16 points from six matches, followed by England on 15 from the same number of games. The eventual outcome is likely to depend on their final meeting in Rome in October.
"This was a very imoportant win for us" said England coach Glenn Hoddle afterwards.

"Our intention has always been to win the group and we can still do that as a result of winning here tonight. Our tactics were right, our attitude was right and it was a very tough match, but we deserved to win it."
England skipper Shearer said: "We thoroughly deserved to win and get the three points. It was a totally professional performance from us and we did what we had to do."

Polish coach Antoni Piechniczek said: "We lost a lot of our composure after their first goal. We are very disappointed, but England are a very good team and could go on and win the group. They will definitely reach the finals."
While much of Europe has been basking in sweltering heat, Poland has been seized by an icy, wintry grip for the last few days and the match was played in freezing, rainy weather.
But England forgot about the chill after only five minutes when Shearer, the world's most expensive striker, scored a goal of true world class quality.

A four-man move from deep inside England's half was started by Gareth Southgate and continued by Robert Lee and Paul Ince, who found Shearer with a long through ball. Shearer, in space, latched on to it, outpaced the defence and curved home his right-footed drive inside the far post.
Poland struggled to recover from that, and could make no real impression on the match even when England playmaker Paul Gascoigne went off with a gashed thigh after 17 minutes.
The Poles did not have a shot on target until the 30th minute but the closest they came to scoring was when Southgate cleared away a goal-bound shot from Jacek Dembinski after 42 minutes.

Three minutes after that Shearer had a golden opportunity to seal the victory when he won a penalty after being fouled by Adam Ledworn but, with the last kick of the first half, he shot against the post.
"It was the first penalty I have ever missed for England, but there is always a first time I suppose," he said.

The second half was a war of attrition with England battling to hold their lead against a Polish attack which never made any real impact against a defence in which Southgate, Sol Campbell and Gary Neville played superbly.
And after Poland lost playmaker Piotr Nowak midway through the second half, their cause was lost and England gave the scoreline some much-deserved respectability with Sheringham's last minute goal.
England easily broke up another Polish attack, and Robert Lee found himself clear of the defence with only goalkeeper Andrzej Wozniak to beat.
Although by the time he had rounded him Polish defenders had moved back, he squared to Sheringham who made no mistake from close range.
